title: Quantum Sensing Beyond Exceptional Points via Hidden symmetry-protected vacuum-noise fixed point
authors: Wencong Wang, Yuyang Liang, Peng Han, Xianqiu Wu, Dongmei Liu, Min Gu
abstract: Exceptional-point (EP) sensing has attracted considerable interest because of its anomalous response scaling. However, recent studies have shown that the enhanced response near an EP is inevitably accompanied by amplified quantum noise, fundamentally limiting the achievable signalto-noise ratio (SNR). Here, we propose a fundamentally different route toward non-Hermitian quantum sensing based on symmetry-protected noise suppression rather than response amplification. We develop a fully quantum continuous-variable model that unifies parity-time (PT) and anti-paritytime(APT) symmetries within a single framework. Exploiting the incompatibility between these two symmetries, we uncover a non-Hermitian Dirac eigenspectrum and reveal a hidden symmetryprotected phase transition embedded in the Hamiltonian spectrum. Remarkably, this hidden phasetransition simultaneously constitutes a symmetry-protected vacuum-noise fixed point, where collective three-mode quadratures exhibit suppressed quantum fluctuations despite the absence of any anomalous spectral response. As a consequence, quantum sensing is enhanced through the suppression of excess quantum noise while maintaining a finite response sensitivity, establishing a sensing mechanism fundamentally different from conventional EP-based approaches. These results reveal an unexpected connection between hidden symmetry, quantum fluctuations, and non-Hermitian quantum metrology, and establish noise suppression as an alternative paradigm for non-Hermitian quantum sensing.
summary: This paper proposes a new paradigm for non-Hermitian quantum sensing by exploiting hidden symmetries rather than relying on exceptional points. Using a continuous-variable model unifying PT and APT symmetries, the authors demonstrate that at a symmetry-protected vacuum-noise fixed point, collective quantum noise is actively suppressed below the vacuum level. This results in enhanced quantum sensing sensitivity through noise control, establishing a distinct theoretical route for quantum metrology.
main_problem: To develop a quantum sensing mechanism that surpasses the fundamental limitation of enhanced sensitivity near Exceptional Points (EPs) being accompanied by amplified quantum noise, thereby limiting the Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR).
main_result: The authors propose an alternative paradigm where quantum sensing is enhanced through the symmetry-protected suppression of excess quantum noise, achieved at a hidden symmetry-protected vacuum-noise fixed point (VFP). This mechanism maintains finite response sensitivity while achieving superior SNR compared to conventional EP approaches.
method: The study employs a fully quantum continuous-variable model and analyzes the system's eigenspectrum derived from an effective Hamiltonian exhibiting a non-Hermitian Dirac structure. The key diagnostic involves calculating the variance of collective quadratures relative to vacuum noise.
model_or_system: The physical model is a three-mode bosonic system coupling degenerate phase-sensitive amplification and detuned non-degenerate parametric processes, unifying Parity-Time (PT) and Anti-Parity-Time (APT) symmetries. The dynamics are analyzed using Heisenberg–Langevin equations leading to an effective Hamiltonian $H_{eff}$ possessing a hidden chiral symmetry.
key_observables: Unitless sensitivity $S(O, 	heta)$, collective quadrature variances ($\Delta P_3^2 / 3$), and the identification of the symmetry-protected vacuum-noise fixed point (VFP).
important_parameters: Detuning ($\delta$), nonlinear coupling ($\kappa_{PT}$), amplification gain ($g$), and linear coupling ($\kappa_{APT}$). The critical regime is defined by balancing these symmetries.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the system can be realized on an integrated photonic platform, maintaining standard bosonic commutation relations without needing to explicitly include additional Langevin noise terms in the Heisenberg equations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the evolution of the non-Hermitian Dirac eigenspectrum under balanced symmetries and show that the quantum fluctuation variance ($\Delta P_3^2 / 3$) is squeezed below vacuum noise at the symmetry-protected point, while sensitivity metrics peak there.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the problem with EPs. It then develops a unified PT/APT continuous-variable model and analyzes its non-Hermitian Dirac eigenspectrum. The core of the work involves demonstrating that at a specific hidden symmetry-protected point, quantum noise is suppressed (VFP), leading to enhanced sensing performance distinct from EP enhancement.
why_interesting: This work provides a novel theoretical framework for quantum metrology by shifting focus from spectral anomalies (EPs) to fundamental symmetries protecting the vacuum state. It connects topological concepts (hidden symmetry, Dirac spectrum) directly to noise control in open quantum systems, which is highly relevant to AMO and quantum optics.
